summary: Object-storage + lead-attachments feature (iteration 56) verified end-to-end. Backend: 15/15 pytest tests pass against the real Emergent object storage — profile upload (round-trip, PDF/oversize/unauth rejects), document upload (staff 403, admin OK, MIME/size rejects, bad lead scope 404), lead attach → serve → detach → cascade, soft-delete-by-id, serve auth (bearer + ?auth=, bad token 401). Frontend: super_admin can open LeadDetailDialog, sees lead-attachments panel, upload button + hidden input, PDF upload creates lead-attachment-<id> row with lead-attachment-dl-* (containing ?auth=<token>) + lead-attachment-del-*; window.confirm delete removes the row. Storage paths conform to spec (finflow/uploads/{user_id}/… and finflow/leads/{lead_id}/…).
critical_code_review_comments: Minor: routers/leads.py::attach_document uses require_edit('leads') then _require_admin — staff with leads=edit hit the same 403 path, which is fine, but the double dependency slightly muddles intent. Consider a single `require_admin` dependency for symmetry with uploads.py.
Minor: LeadAttachments.jsx uses `FilePdf` from @phosphor-icons/react — confirmed to render without runtime error, but note this alias only exists in newer versions; pin version if bumping.
Nit: no GET /api/leads/{id} endpoint; tests had to fall back to list-and-filter. Fine for now but adding a single-lead fetch would be tidy.
storage.py `init_storage` is not thread/async safe (global mutation via requests, blocking) — acceptable at current scale but flag for future refactor to httpx + asyncio.Lock.
